prerequisites: Basic knowledge from introductory lectures "Chemistry" and "Physics"
Basic knowledge in Chemistry and Physics (for Materials Science 1)

learning_outcomes.text: Students can derive relationships between the atomic solid-state structure, the microscopic microstructure, and the material properties based on the acquired knowledge about structural and functional materials.
They can apply learned formulas and solve simple problems.
They are able to read subject-specific diagrams and formulate the result in writing and/or orally.
They can read and interpret material designations and are able to deduce resulting properties and possible uses of materials.
Students are able to qualitatively and quantitatively assess fundamental materials science questions independently or in a team, and thus apply the theoretically acquired knowledge in practice.
Knowledge of the dependencies of "manufacturing, microstructure and properties" enables them to familiarize themselves with previously unknown topics in materials science.

syllabus_topics: Main material groups, microstructure and properties, material selection
Atomic structure, crystalline and non-crystalline (amorphous) atomic arrangements, lattice defects
Alloy theory
Phase transformations in pure metals, recovery and recrystallization behavior
Materials testing
Fundamentals of heat treatment
Important standards for steel and iron
Non-ferrous metals
Magnetism
Ceramic materials
Composite materials
Knowledge of structural materials and (less extensively) functional materials
Understanding the relationships between atomic solid-state structure, microscopic observations, and material properties
Assessment of properties and resulting applications
Properties of various materials based on atomic structure and lattice defects
Manufacturing of materials and knowledge of important phase diagrams, especially the "iron-carbon diagram"
Basic materials testing procedures: tensile test, hardness test, impact bending test, fatigue test
Knowledge of possible material damages (e.g., corrosion) and their prevention
Methods for non-destructive materials testing
Variation of material properties through targeted thermal, thermo-mechanical, and thermo-chemical treatments, focusing on steels and latest developments
Light metals: aluminum, magnesium, titanium and their alloys
Special properties of non-ferrous metals, hard metals, shape memory alloys, and ceramic materials
Basic knowledge of magnetic materials, their different properties and application areas
assessment_rules: Credits are awarded when the module final examination is passed and qualified participation (Fachgespräch: 20-30 minutes) is demonstrated. In the exam, students must establish connections between structure, properties, and use of materials, name and describe appropriate material testing methods, read subject-specific diagrams and extract important quantities for calculations, perform calculations, describe materials science processes, and justify the use of materials for specific applications.
